headerDisplay:
**Quick setup**
1. In UniFi OS → **Settings → Control Plane → Integrations**, create an **API Key** and paste it below.
2. Enter your console's address (the same one you use for the UniFi web app).
3. *(Optional, for arm/disarm)* In **Protect → Alarm Manager**, create webhook-triggered alarms with an **Arm** or **Disarm** action, and paste each **Trigger ID** below.
4. Save & restart. Your zones, hub and outputs are discovered automatically.
footerDisplay: Outputs and the emergency input are read-only (UniFi does not yet allow controlling them via the API). See the [README](https://github.com/actravis/homebridge-unifi-protect-alarm-hub) for details.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name shown for this platform in Homebridge logs.

host.title: UniFi Console Address
host.description: IP or hostname of your UDM / Cloud Key / NVR — the same address you use for the UniFi web app.

apiKey.title: API Key
apiKey.description: Create it in UniFi OS → Settings → Control Plane → Integrations, then paste it here. This key grants console-wide access — treat it like a password.

securityName.title: Alarm tile name
securityName.description: Name for the alarm accessory in HomeKit (e.g. "Security System" or "Security").

armAwayTriggerId.title: "Away" arm — webhook Trigger ID
armAwayTriggerId.description: In Alarm Manager create an alarm: Trigger = Webhook, Action = Arm → Away. Paste its Trigger ID here. Leave blank if you don't use Away.

armNightTriggerId.title: "Night" arm — webhook Trigger ID
armNightTriggerId.description: Same, but Action = Arm → Night. Leave blank if you don't use Night.

disarmTriggerId.title: Disarm — webhook Trigger ID
disarmTriggerId.description: Same, but Action = Disarm. Leave all three blank and the alarm tile shows status but can't be changed from HomeKit.

exposeAlarm.title: Expose alarm accessories
exposeAlarm.description: Master switch for the alarm domain (security system, hub, zones, outputs, emergency input). Turn off to expose cameras only. Note: disabling does not remove accessories already added to HomeKit.

glassBreakAs.title: Show glass-break sensors as
glassBreakAs.description: HomeKit has no native glass-break type.

exposeOutputs.title: Expose alarm-hub outputs
exposeOutputs.description: Shows outputs (e.g. the Beeper) as read-only sensors. UniFi does not yet allow controlling them from HomeKit.

exposeEmergencyInput.title: Expose emergency input
exposeEmergencyInput.description: Shows the emergency terminal as a read-only sensor.

sirenOutputChannels.title: Siren output channel(s)
sirenOutputChannels.description: Which output channel(s) mean a real alarm, for the "triggered" state (comma-separated, 1-indexed to match UniFi). Leave blank to treat any active output as triggered.

exposeCameras.title: Expose cameras
exposeCameras.description: Create a motion sensor (and a doorbell for doorbell cameras) per camera, driven by the realtime feed. If you also run another UniFi Protect plugin, disable its motion/doorbell to avoid duplicates.

exposeObjectSensors.title: Expose smart-detection sensors
exposeObjectSensors.description: Add a separate motion sensor per smart-detect type each camera supports (person, vehicle, animal, package) for use in automations.

exposeAudioSensors.title: Expose smoke / CO alarm sensors (experimental)
exposeAudioSensors.description: Adds a native HomeKit smoke and/or carbon-monoxide sensor per camera, driven by Protect’s audio detection — it reports that the camera HEARD an alarm, and is not a detector itself. Useful because a sounding alarm then becomes a HomeKit trigger (lights on, notifications). Only detections you have enabled in Protect are exposed. Experimental: the event shape has not yet been confirmed on real hardware, so if your alarm sounds and the sensor stays clear, please report it with debug logging on.

exposeDoorbellTriggers.title: Add doorbell-trigger switches
exposeDoorbellTriggers.description: Add a "Doorbell Trigger" switch to every camera. Flip it from an automation to ring the doorbell — e.g. when your driveway camera detects a vehicle. Any camera becomes ringable (gains a doorbell notification).

doorbellDeviceIds.title: Force these cameras to be doorbells
doorbellDeviceIds.description: Optional. Doorbells are detected automatically; add a camera's device ID here if one is missed (the log names the ID when a ring arrives from a camera not detected as a doorbell).

exposeCameraStreams.title: Show cameras as HomeKit cameras
exposeCameraStreams.description: Attach a HomeKit camera to each camera: live video, snapshots, and snapshots in motion/doorbell notifications. Video is transcoded from the camera's RTSPS stream by ffmpeg. Camera audio is not streamed yet. Turn this off to expose cameras as motion sensors only (no ffmpeg, no video).

exposeCameraAudio.title: Stream camera audio (experimental)
exposeCameraAudio.description: Include the camera microphone in the live stream. Needs an ffmpeg that can encode a codec HomeKit accepts — AAC-ELD (libfdk_aac) or Opus (libopus); the bundled ffmpeg provides Opus. The plugin tests this at startup and logs which codec it chose, or falls back to video-only if neither works. Experimental: audio changes how iOS negotiates the stream, so if live view stops working, turn this off first.

refreshInterval.title: Fallback refresh interval (seconds)
refreshInterval.description: How often to re-check alarm state. While the realtime push feed is connected this is automatically backed off to 60 seconds (or this value, whichever is longer), since every change already arrives as a push; the full rate resumes if the feed drops. Only lower it if you run with realtime updates turned off.

useRealtime.title: Use realtime updates
useRealtime.description: Recommended. Uses the console's push feed for ~1–2s updates, falling back to the interval above.

realtimeIdleTimeout.title: Realtime idle timeout (seconds, 0 = off)
realtimeIdleTimeout.description: Advanced. Force a reconnect if the realtime feed is silent this long. Off by default: this API sends no keepalives, so silence usually just means nothing happened, and dead connections are already caught by TCP keepalive. Only enable if your system has reliably frequent events and you want an extra backstop.

trustSelfSignedCert.title: Trust console certificate
trustSelfSignedCert.description: UniFi consoles use self-signed certificates. When on, the plugin trusts this specific console. Leave on unless you've installed your own valid certificate.

certificateSha256.title: Pin certificate (SHA-256)
certificateSha256.description: Optional, most secure. Paste the console's certificate SHA-256 fingerprint (64 hex characters, colons optional) to pin it. When set, only that exact certificate is accepted and the setting above is ignored. A malformed value stops the plugin rather than silently falling back to no pinning.
